name: Summer Homework
description: By the age of three Smart Beaver mastered all arithmetic operations and got this summer homework from the amazed teacher: You are given a sequence of integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . Your task is to perform on it m consecutive operations of the following type: For given numbers x i and v i assign value v i to element a x i . For given numbers l i and r i you've got to calculate sum , where f 0 = f 1 = 1 and at i ≥ 2 : f i = f i - 1 + f i - 2 . For a group of three numbers l i r i d i you should increase value a x by d i for all x ( l i ≤ x ≤ r i ) . Smart Beaver planned a tour around great Canadian lakes, so he asked you to help him solve the given problem.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers n and m ( 1 ≤ n , m ≤ 2·10 5 ) — the number of integers in the sequence and the number of operations, correspondingly. The second line contains n integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n ( 0 ≤ a i ≤ 10 5 ). Then follow m lines, each describes an operation. Each line starts with an integer t i ( 1 ≤ t i ≤ 3 ) — the operation type: if t i = 1 , then next follow two integers x i v i ( 1 ≤ x i ≤ n , 0 ≤ v i ≤ 10 5 ); if t i = 2 , then next follow two integers l i r i ( 1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ n ); if t i = 3 , then next follow three integers l i r i d i ( 1 ≤ l i ≤ r i ≤ n , 0 ≤ d i ≤ 10 5 ). The input limits for scoring 30 points are (subproblem E1): It is guaranteed that n does not exceed 100 , m does not exceed 10000 and there will be no queries of the 3 -rd type. The input limits for scoring 70 points are (subproblems E1+E2): It is guaranteed that there will be queries of the 1 -st and 2 -nd type only. The input limits for scoring 100 points are (subproblems E1+E2+E3): No extra limitations.
output_specification: For each query print the calculated sum modulo 1000000000 (10 9 ) .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 316E2 — Summer Homework [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
